clue.text: Children returning with a beast from Africa

indicators.note: returning tells us to turn each of the two pieces round where it stands

parts.note: a kid is a child, and children are two kids
the second of the two kids that children supplies

explanation.surface: Youngsters come home from a trip with an African animal in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns each piece round where it stands; 'Children' has to supply two of the same young goat word.
explanation.definitionFit: The dik-dik is a tiny antelope native to the scrub of eastern and southern Africa.

clue.text: Jo's bottle?

parts.note: the short name Jo is half of a longer man's name, and a half-version of that name gives a large wicker-covered flask

explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a big narrow-necked bottle used for wine or home brewing.

clue.text: We rank it exceptional for warmth

definitions.note: a phrase of purpose standing for the woollen garments themselves

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the letters are made unusual by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone rates a thing outstanding for keeping out the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' rearranges WE RANK IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpers and cardigans are made to keep the wearer warm.

clue.text: It's best to stride along if weak

indicators.note: weak suggests only a diluted portion of the words is wanted, the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Advice to keep walking when you feel feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'stride along'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is perfect, the best possible.

clue.text: Companion, a body with-out second companion

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: with-out, split with a hyphen, is just 'without': the letter for second is dropped from the body

parts.note: a body is a person, as in 'a nice old body'

explanation.surface: A wordy definition of a chaperon as someone who keeps company with another body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with-out' removes S (second) from PERSON, leaving PERON; CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is a person who accompanies and supervises another, so is a kind of minder or escort.

clue.text: Fruit of melody, when one is composed

indicators.note: is composed suggests the words are arranged afresh, like music

explanation.surface: A tune is the fruit of creativity once written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is composed' rearranges MELODY WHEN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sweet melon with pale green flesh.

clue.text: One sick almost died without something to rest on

indicators.note: without in the old sense of 'outside'
almost cuts the last letter from the word for died

parts.note: passed means died
A means one
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone ill nearly died for lack of a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PASSED to PASSE; 'without' puts that outside A ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A paillasse is a straw-filled mattress, so a bed to lie on.

clue.text: Condition of 12

parts.note: 12 across is a tenancy agreement, and a key condition of one is the payment due for it

explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the payment a tenant makes, a term of any tenancy agreement.

clue.text: Number's up — Roger's gripped with apprehension

indicators.note: gripped says the number holds the letter inside
up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: seven is a number
Roger is the radio code word for R

explanation.surface: A number is up, and a man called Roger is seized with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEVEN into NEVES, which 'gripped' wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves means anxiety or fearful tension before an ordeal.

clue.text: State without a pit

indicators.note: without in the old sense of 'outside': the pit goes round the A

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A US state that has no mining industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: MINE sits outside A.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA.

clue.text: One ripens in order to qualify

definitions.text: One ripens in order to qualify

indicators.note: in order says the letters are to be put into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: A person grows older until eligible for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges the letters of ONE RIPENS; the whole clue also describes ageing until you qualify for a state pension.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person drawing a state pension, which you only qualify for by reaching a certain age.

clue.text: Permit for sale of spirits and ale

definitions.text: Permit for sale of spirits and ale

parts.words: Permit for sale of spirits and ale
parts.note: reads as a drinks licence, but the spirit wanted is the creative one that lets a writer bend rules

explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom allowed to poets to depart from fact or grammar.

clue.text: Adornment for Israelite Queen

parts.note: an Israelite is a Jew
Ellery Queen is the pen name and detective hero of American crime novels

explanation.surface: A piece of finery chosen for a Jewish queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is not a monarch but the surname of Ellery Queen, the US detective-fiction pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings, necklaces and brooches are worn as ornament, so jewellery is personal decoration.

clue.text: Student finds relief in getting hold of accommodation

definitions.note: a phrase about acquiring; the answer is the verb for obtaining a property this way

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate, standing for a student
ease is relief from pain or care

explanation.surface: A student is relieved to secure somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease is to take a property for a fixed term in return for rent, which is how a tenant secures housing.

clue.text: Complaint of girl taken in by pansy

indicators.note: taken in by says the girl is placed inside the flower

parts.note: heartsease is the wild pansy
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A girl is fooled by an effeminate man and complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pansy' is not a slur here but the flower heartsease; 'taken in by' puts DI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart disease is an illness, and a complaint can mean an ailment.

clue.text: Try while there's time to get in one's last word

definitions.text: Try while there's time to get in one's last word

parts.note: to test is to try
amen is the last word of a prayer

explanation.surface: Get your will written while you still have time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes writing a will before it is too late, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, a person's final statement of wishes.

clue.text: Like beauty of a sort with ooze about it

indicators.note: about it says the ooze surrounds the sort

parts.note: to seep is to ooze
a kind is a sort

explanation.surface: A dubious beauty treatment involving some oozing substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is that beauty is only skin-deep, that is superficial; 'about it' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that beauty is only superficial, going no further than the surface.

clue.text: There's an alternative to force and that's material

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
G is the symbol for gravitational force
i.e. stands for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Another way to use force, which is the substance of the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine stiff transparent cotton fabric.

clue.text: Luke sees Mary, perhaps, as one seldom given due welcome

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these names might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: In a Bible-flavoured scene Luke catches sight of Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of LUKE SEES MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Refugees seeking sanctuary are often met with suspicion, so they rarely receive the welcome owed them.

clue.text: No firm ground for men in service

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the service

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers serving are not on solid footing.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is military shorthand for enlisted men.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog, wet land too soft to stand on.

clue.text: Item: the devil's in it

definitions.meaning: from the saying that the devil is in the small particulars

explanation.definitionFit: A detail is one small particular, and the proverb puts trouble there.

clue.text: Ring? Perhaps get a representative to ring back

indicators.note: back turns the whole string of pieces round

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Is it a ring? Maybe phone an agent to return the call.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring is Wagner's cycle of operas; 'back' turns A REP O round. 'ring' in the wordplay is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring cycle is a set of operas, so the Ring is an example of the genre, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Scotland starts criticising English fellow, inter alia

indicators.note: starts picks out the opening letter of criticising
inter is Latin for 'among', so the Englishman goes inside alia

parts.note: a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: Scotland begins finding fault with, among other things, an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' is Latin for 'among other things', but here 'inter' puts EDON among the letters of ALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, still used poetically.

clue.text: Friday's writer

parts.note: Friday is not a weekday but Man Friday, Crusoe's companion, so the author of Robinson Crusoe

explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, in which the servant Friday appears.

clue.text: Game no man played without old king

indicators.note: played suggests the words are moved about like pieces in a game

explanation.surface: A game nobody played, lacking a historic monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges GAME NO MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Strife about right as inspirer of sexy slips

indicators.note: about says the strife goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a feud is bitter strife

explanation.surface: Fighting over who rightly caused some saucy lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' are not underwear but slips of the tongue, revealing hidden desires.
explanation.definitionFit: The psychoanalyst gave his name to the Freudian slip, an error said to reveal a sexual urge.

clue.text: It separates having no offspring and several

parts.note: SP is sine prole, Latin for 'without issue', used in genealogy
a litter is several young born together

explanation.surface: A divorce story about a couple with no children and then many.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole) is a genealogists' abbreviation meaning childless.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or person that divides things, such as a log cleaver, does the job of parting.

clue.text: Pattern, a model apart, for an archbishop

indicators.note: apart says the model is taken away from the pattern

parts.note: a template is a pattern to cut round
A and T, as in the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a model of an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' takes A and T (from the Model T Ford) out of TEMPLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: William Temple and his father Frederick were both Archbishops of Canterbury.
